finding.claim: Unauthenticated SSRF: attacker-supplied POST 'feed' is passed unvalidated to file_get_contents(), which accepts http(s)://, file://, and php:// wrappers. Response returns only strlen(), so the bug is blind SSRF with a length oracle.
finding.source: import.php:11 — $_POST['feed'] (no auth; only REQUEST_METHOD===POST and isset checks)

trace.note: Branch runs for any POST with 'feed' set; no session or require_admin() check before it
Raw user value passed to file_get_contents(); no scheme, host, IP, or redirect validation
Only strlen($xml) is echoed; body is not returned, so exploitation is blind

finding.guards_checked: Request method check and isset() only. No scheme allowlist, no private/loopback/link-local/metadata IP blocking, no redirect control, no allow_url_fopen or open_basedir enforcement in code. Precondition: allow_url_fopen=On for remote schemes (default); file:// works regardless. Deployment php.ini not verified.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only check before the sink is the POST method test and isset() at import.php:11. require_admin() is defined at import.php:4-9 but is not called on that branch; it is only called at import.php:18 for set_webhook. No scheme, host, IP, or redirect validation exists before file_get_contents() at import.php:12.
verdict.reason: The attacker-controlled $_POST['feed'] reaches file_get_contents() at import.php:12 with no authentication or validation, and the response only exposes strlen($xml) at import.php:13, so the candidate's trace is accurate and the bug is blind SSRF/file read with a length oracle; remote http(s) depends on allow_url_fopen, but file:// works regardless, and that deployment setting was not verified.
